title: Optimized protocol for DNA/RNA co-extraction from adults of Dirofilaria immitis
author: Lucchetti, Genchi, et al.
materials: Following owners’ consent, 12 adult worms of D. immitis, respectively 6 females and 6 males, were collected during minimally-invasive surgical heartworm removal from two dogs previously diagnosed with patent D. immitis infection. Extracted worms were washed in Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution medium (Sigma-Aldrich®, Missouri, USA) at room temperature, checked for viability, counted and sexed. Three female and three male worms were individually placed into 15 mL Falcon tubes and stored at −80 °C. Single worms were used as starting material for the RNA/DNA co-extraction.

Therefore, a solution of 150 ng/μL of RNA in a final volume of 50 μL was prepared for each sample. To each sample, 5 μL of TURBO™ DNase buffer and 2 μL of TURBO™ DNase (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, USA) were added, followed by incubation at 37 °C for 30 min. After the first incubation, a further 2 μL of TURBO™ DNase enzyme was added and incubated again at 37 °C for other 30 min.

To obtain a fully pure RNA sample to be used for gene expression analysis, an additional purification step was performed. RNA samples were treated with AccuRT Genomic DNA Removal Kit (Abm, Richmond, Canada) according to the manufacturer protocol. Starting with 300 ng of final RNA, and followed by an incubation at room temperature of 8 min. For cDNA synthesis, the OneScript® cDNA Synthesis Kit (Abm, Richmond, Canada) was used. The presence of any genomic contamination was checked by PCR reaction using GOTAQ Flexi DNA Polymerase Green G2 (Fisher MB, Rome, Italy) and 0.35 μM of specific primers designed on Dim-pgp-10 for cDNA (DimmScaf48-cDNA-F8: 5′-GCCATCGTAGGTCCATCAGGTTCTGGT-3′; DimmScaf48-cDNA-R12: 5′-TGTTCAACTGAAACGACCACACGTC-3′) (Sigma-Aldrich®, Missouri, USA) [2]. The amplification protocol was characterized by a denaturation step at 95 °C for 1,30 min, followed by 40 repeated cycles: 95 °C for 15 s; 59.4 °C for 1 min with a final elongation of 72 °C for 5 min. Amplicons were run on a 2% agarose gel. For pure cDNA only one band would be of 155bp while in presence of genomic DNA contamination a second band of amplification would be visible at 476bp.

To validate the efficiency of proposed protocol, RNA products obtained with the just described protocol were compared to those obtained with the use of a product specific for the optimization and simplification of RNA isolation: Phasemaker™ Tubes (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, USA).

steps.title: Collect and store adult worms
steps.instruction: Obtain 12 adult Dirofilaria immitis worms (6 females, 6 males) during minimally‑invasive heartworm removal, wash each in Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution at room temperature, check viability, count and sex, place three females and three males individually into 15 mL Falcon tubes and store at –80 °C; use a single worm as the starting material for each co‑extraction.

steps.title: Add TRIzol to homogenized worm
steps.instruction: To each tube containing 500 µL of homogenized worm sample add 500 µL of TRIzol® reagent and process according to the TRIzol® manufacturer’s protocol up to phase separation.

steps.title: Separate aqueous phase and repeat isolation
steps.instruction: After the three phases separate, carefully transfer the aqueous phase to a new tube and repeat the isolation steps as described by the manufacturer, applying the same protocol for both RNA and DNA but using the modified elution conditions described below.

steps.title: Elute RNA
steps.instruction: Elute the RNA in 100 µL of DEPC‑treated water, then place the tube in a water bath at 56 °C for 13 min; if the pellet is larger, extend the incubation at 56 °C until the pellet is fully rehydrated.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Elute the DNA in 300 µL of DEPC‑treated water and incubate the tube in a water bath at 46 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: Vortex and quantify nucleic acids
steps.instruction: Briefly vortex each resuspended sample, then measure concentration (ng/µL) and purity (260/280 and 260/230 ratios) using a BioSpectrometer® fluorescence spectrophotometer with μCuvetta® G 1.0 (Eppendorf, Hamburg, Germany).

steps.title: DNase treatment of RNA
steps.instruction: Prepare a solution of 150 ng/µL RNA in a final volume of 50 µL for each sample; add 5 µL TURBO™ DNase buffer and 2 µL TURBO™ DNase (Thermo Fisher Scientific), incubate at 37 °C for 30 min; then add an additional 2 µL TURBO™ DNase and incubate again at 37 °C for another 30 min.

steps.title: Second RNA extraction
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of TRIzol® reagent to each DNase‑treated tube and perform a second RNA extraction following the TRIzol® manufacturer protocol; elute the RNA in 35 µL of DEPC water and rehydrate the pellet at 56 °C for 13 min (or longer if needed). Quantify the RNA again with the spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Genomic DNA removal for cDNA synthesis
steps.instruction: Treat 300 ng of the final RNA with the AccuRT Genomic DNA Removal Kit (Abm, Richmond, Canada) according to the kit protocol and incubate at room temperature for 8 min.

steps.title: cDNA synthesis
steps.instruction: Synthesize cDNA from the DNase‑treated RNA using the OneScript® cDNA Synthesis Kit (Abm, Richmond, Canada) following the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Check for genomic DNA contamination
steps.instruction: Perform PCR with GOTAQ Flexi DNA Polymerase Green G2 (Fisher MB, Rome, Italy) using 0.35 µM primers DimmScaf48‑cDNA‑F8 (5′‑GCCATCGTAGGTCCATCAGGTTCTGGT‑3′) and DimmScaf48‑cDNA‑R12 (5′‑TGTTCAACTGAAACGACCACACGTC‑3′); run the program: 95 °C 1.30 min; 40 cycles of 95 °C 15 s, 59.4 °C 1 min; final extension 72 °C 5 min. Resolve products on a 2 % agarose gel; a single 155 bp band indicates pure cDNA, while an additional 476 bp band indicates genomic DNA contamination.

steps.title: Optional validation with Phasemaker™ Tubes
steps.instruction: For comparison, process three adult worms per sex using Phasemaker™ Tubes (Thermo Fisher Scientific) according to the manufacturer’s protocol (two samples per female, one per male). Process the remaining samples with the co‑extraction protocol described above and compare RNA yield and purity.
